messages.text: Start with your checks: which of your pieces can give check right now? Then look at their king: if it is attacked, where could it go?
Look at their king on g8: it is boxed in by its own pawns on f7, g7 and h7. Their rook is also far away on a8. What could you do on that back row?

outcomes.detail: Rd8+ is the strongest move: it gives check, and it forces checkmate in 2. After Rxd8 Rxd8, their king is stuck behind its own pawns. That's a back-rank mate. When their king is shut in by its pawns, check every check on the last rank first.

outcomes.detail: Nc7+ is the strongest move: it gives check, and you win a rook. This is a fork: one piece attacks two things at once, here the king and the rook on a8. The king must move, then Nxa8 takes the rook. To spot it next time, look at your checks first and ask what else the checking piece attacks.
